item: OSM daily change files: fetch, apply atomically per file, re-baseline past retention (v0.6.0 B1, S06-01 S1)
key_paths: src/osm/replication.py; src/osm/apply.py; src/osm/changes.py; src/osm/lane_models.py; src/osm/geometry.py; src/osm/ingest.py; scripts/make_osm_fixture.py; tests/test_osm_apply.py
summary: A country cut from a Geofabrik extract can now be brought forward by the mirror's daily change files: the URL is built from the download manager's host and a validated region code (never read from a file header), the session refuses any other host on every hop, and a kill switch / transport / 404 / network failure each say which they were. Each file applies in ONE transaction with the position, the substrate cursor and a run row (rolled back whole on any failure); only the kept classes change, an older version never overwrites, a way whose vertices cannot all be found is never placed and keeps its stored shape, a relation is placed by the border or a stored member, and objects that left a class or the border are deleted and counted. A country whose first owed file is past the ~3 month retention (or whose mirror no longer holds it) is re-cut from a fresh extract and a retention gap is published; a hand re-cut that disagrees with the cursor publishes a budget gap. The staleness basis of the derived tables moves with the diff position (country_basis), and the search and view indexes are rebuilt after a run. Fixture-only: the layout is from memory and the network was unreachable, so the operator row in RELEASE_0.6_GATE confirms it; no tag-change rows (B2), no trend surface (B3), no UI/job layer yet (follow-on bundle).
